abstract: Browser automation CLI for AI agentshttps://agent-browser.devagent-browser Browser automation for AI agents: open pages, read them as an accessibility tree, and act on elements from the shell. agent-browser is a native Rust CLI that gives an AI agent a browser it can drive one command at a time. snapshot returns the page as compact text with a ref such as @e1 for each element. The agent acts on a ref, reads the page again to check the result, and repeats. The browser stays open between commands, so each step is one short shell call. Install npm install -g agent-browser agent-browser install # download Chrome for Testing (first time only) Homebrew: brew install agent-browser, then agent-browser install. headline: lz4/lz4
abstract: Extremely Fast Compression algorithmhttp://www.lz4.orgLZ4 - Extremely fast compression LZ4 is a lossless compression algorithm, providing compression speed > 500 MB/s per core, scalable with multi-core CPUs. It features an extremely fast decoder, with speed in multiple GB/s per core, typically reaching RAM speed limits on multi-core systems. Compression speed can be tuned dynamically, by selecting an "acceleration" factor which trades compression ratio for faster speed. On the other end, a high compression derivative, LZ4_HC, is also provided, trading CPU time for improved compression ratio. All versions feature the same decompression speed. LZ4 is also compatible with dictionary compression, both at API and CLI (-D) levels. It can ingest any input file as dictionary, though only the final 64 KB are used. This capability can be combined with the Zstandard Dictionary Builder, in order to drastically improve compression performance on small files. The LZ4 library is provided as open-source software using the BSD 2-Clause license. The lz4 command line utility is provided under the GPL-2.0-or-later license. Benchmarks The benchmark uses lzbench v2.4.1, from @inikep compiled with GCC v13.3.0 on Linux 64-bits (Ubuntu 24.04). The reference system uses a Core i7-9700K CPU.
